'''Virginia Halmos''' (1915–2015), born Virginia Pritchett, was an American philanthropist who supported mathematics research. She and her husband [[Paul Halmos]] endowed the [[American Mathematical Society]]'s [[Joseph L. Doob Prize]] for research exposition.<ref name=DoobPrize>{{cite web|title=Joseph L. Doob Prize|website=American Mathematical Society|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-prizes/doob-prize|access-date=2024-12-07|archive-date=2019-03-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190311064329/http://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-prizes/doob-prize|url-status=dead}}</ref> They also made substantial gifts to the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name="focus obit">{{cite news |title=Virginia Halmos dies at age 99 |url=https://digitaleditions.walsworth.com/article/Virginia+Halmos+Dies+at+Age+99/1938461/247647/article.html |access-date=7 December 2024 |publisher=MAA Focus |date=February–March 2015}}</ref> In particular, they endowed the Mathematical Association of America's [[Euler Book Prize]], which was first given in 2007.<ref name="jmm07">{{citation|title=JMM 2007: Report of the MAA Secretary|journal=Focus|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|url=http://www.maa.org/pubs/february07web.pdf|first=Martha J.|last=Siegel|authorlink=Martha Siegel|date=February 2007|pages=8–10|access-date=2011-02-02|archive-date=2012-10-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002231341/http://www.maa.org/pubs/february07web.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref> After her husband's death, Virginia Halmos donated funds to the Mathematical Association of America to support digitization of her husband's extensive archives.<ref name="focus archives">{{cite journal |last1=Mead |first1=Carol |title=Virginia Halmos's generosity benefits us all |journal=MAA Focus |date=April–May 2015 }}</ref>

Virginia Halmos (then Pritchett) earned an undergraduate degree at [[Vassar College]]. She went to graduate school at [[Brown University]], where she studied logic. She left the graduate program in 1945 when she married Paul Halmos, but she maintained a strong interest in mathematics and the lives of mathematicians.<ref name="notices obit">{{cite journal |last1=Alexanderson |first1=Gerald |authorlink=Gerald L. Alexanderson |title=Virginia Halmos (1915–2015) |journal=AMS Notices |date=May 2015 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201505/rnoti-p564.pdf |access-date=7 December 2024}}</ref>
